En Route
PERSONAL & CONFIDENTIAL
Manila
June 28, 1935.
22
(w. S. Grooch
(George Rumi1l
(Wm. Ehmer
(P. G. Klauk
OLD CHINA HANDS (Mrs. Dorothy Gast
I have been very neglectful of all correspondence
lately by force of much travel including two trips to Szechuan,
two trips to Peiping, three to Canton, four to Nanking, one to
Kobe and one to Manila, all within the last three months.
that time my log shows
in round figures 12,000 miles by air,
4700 miles by boat, 1300 miles by train, fifty miles by bus,
no record by automobile or ricksha, one mile by sedan chair
and one hundred feet by wheelbarrow - that last was the hardest.
High lights - a night with the missionaries at Kweiyang while
Communists were marching on the town from forty miles away -
in my room a sign surrounded by forget-me-nots - colors slightly
off center like the funny papers - "Motto for the year - He
Spaketh and there was a great Calm. " Outside to the north
firing.
I concluded there must have been some mix up on either
- mottos or years.
Another highlight - a "Foreign" breakfast in
my honor by Chinese friends in Chungking held in the Board room
oT a bank,
time 7 a. m. - menu - tomato soup - tumbler full of
brandy followed by ten courses. Another highlight a trip to
Hongkong to catch boat to Manila leaving same afternoon - picked
up Groeger at Foochow ran out of ceiling at Bias Bay and landed.
You remember how Groeger likes the "Parrots" but no pirates
showed up and the fog lifted in time to make the boat.
Now I'm on the way to Manila again and hope to be there
in time to meet the North Haven with Bill Grooch as C. 0. He will
be amused by a queer coincidence. You remember when we made the
first flight to Canton leaving Shanghai on July 3, 1933 Mr. Bond
got a wire from his old friend Admiral Shen, Mayor of Tsingtao
to the effect that three cruisers of the Northern Fleet had gone
A.O.W.L. and would we keep an eye out for them.
become embroiled in any Chinese politics we all decided that if
we chanced to see them we would just be unable to identify them.
Anyway when we got to Hongkong they had already passed there and
were on their way to Canton where they have remained ever since -
that is until last Saturday.
When I sailed Thursday afternoon
June 20th from Hongkong two of the cruisers were in the harbor.
It's hard to figure it all out but as near as I can learn the
statements and facts regarding their movements are about as
follows: Number One Statement the druisers Hai Shan and Hat Chi
the gunboat Chao Ho all under the command of Admiral Kiang
Shi-yuen revolted from the Northern Fleet in July 1933 and Joined
Canton because of mistreatment on the part of Admiral Shen Hung-leh,
Mayor of Tsingtao (who incidentally got to be Mayor by virtue of
himself having lead a successful navy revolt a few years before
Number One Fact - the officers of the ships thought they could
sell the boats to Canton.
Number Two Statement - The present
withdrawal of the Hai Shan and Hai Chi was because the officers
wished to rejoin the Northern Fleet on account of the North China
Number Two Fact - Canton agreed to pay the officers for
the boats but had never done so and had recently cut wages and
demoted Admiral Kiang to the rank of Rear Admiral thus costing
him face and Canton two cruisers.
Statement Number Three - when
the Hai Chi and the Hai Shan revolted the Chao Ho remained loyal.
Fact Number Three - Friends in Canton told me that the Chao Ho

Page 2
got stuck in the mud when the cruisers left,
and was unable to escape
Statement Number Four - A wounded officer brought into
a Hongkong hospital when the Hai Chi arrived there said the two
cruisers were subjected to a merciless fire from the forts at Bocca
Tigris and were attacked by 100 airplanes which dropped 1000 bombs.
Fact Number Four - One of our aviation friends in Canton told us that
the river at Bocca Tigris is only one half mile wide with the forts
on either side but neither of the ships were hit.
The air force was
turned out but they could only find a few pilots and of the eight
Curtiss Hawks and ten Boeings only four motors could be started and
one of then had & forced lending right after the take off - the other
three had machine guns but the wrong sized ammunition.
They did đr op
52 bombs of which seven exploded but not near enough to the ships to
do any damage.
Statement Number Five - Many dead and wounded on the
two cruisers.
Fact Number Five - One coolie died of friggh - one
sailor got hurt when he fired a grease filled rifle at the forts and
the rifle exploded, one officer was cut by broken glass (probably
when he dove through his stateroom door).
Now the cruisers are in Hongkong coaling presumably for a trip
Maybe the Canton Air Force will attack them again when they
leave Hongkong or maybe the Nanking Government will heed Canton's
request and send the cruiser Haining in pursuit.
The Hai Chi and
Hai Shan were built in 1898 and wouldn't have much of a show against
the new Japanese built Haining acquired only a few years ago - the
pride and joy of the Chinese Navy - which for effectiveness is sur-
passed only by the Swiss Navy.
Maybe you will read some exciting
cable dispatches long before this reaches you.
At any rate this
letter is just within the family and I know that you will keep it
confidential.
CNAC continues to prosper in spite of the growing depression
Western Division Ford is in service from
Chungking to Kweiyang and Yunnan-fu, a four hour flight which equals
24 days by sedan chair. Chiang Kai-shek is in Chengtu beseiged by
office seekers who must use CNAC.
A new Douglas Transport is flying
between Shanghai and Peiping carrying full loads. Eddie Smith has
been home on leave and is back again - also Eric
Just - Allie is on
his way back now after six months away.
Howard Norris is due for
home leave and will be the next pilot to pass Woosung by steamer.
Chili Vaughn and Pop Sellers - the latter now a grandfather - the
former still a bachelor - are pushing the Dolphins up and down the
China Coast with increasing loads and regularity. Bond got married
on May 15th in Peiping - the new addition to the CNAC family being
a Miss Katherine Dunlop late of Washington, D. C. She is very at-
tractive and in a few months more will have Bondy *kanu thoroughly
house broken.
Groeger is still riding herd on the coolies who man
the barges on the Shanghai Canton line.
Soldinsky is still cooing
soothing words to his Chinese mechanies and keeping the Dolphins in
A No. l condition.
Mr. Mow, as Miss Forbes puts it, "still l00ks
dumb and comes out with the right answer." We have a new passenger
station at Lunghwa built by the City which is very attractive.
I appreciate the replies which you all sent to my last
cireular letter and take this form of thanking you.
Will try to
the next China news letter a bit sooner than this one followed
All of the Shanghailanders would join in kindest regards
to you all if they knew I was writing.
sincerely,
V.M. Buphy.

properties.sfomuseum:description: Typewritten letter from Harold M. Bixby to W. [William] S. Grooch, George Rumill [Rumrill], Wm. [William] Ehmer, P.G. Klauk, and Mrs. Dorothy Gast (grouped as “Old China hands”), dated June 22, 1935, en route to Manila; marked “Personal & confidential”; includes description of events around three river cruisers / boats, originally referenced in 2019.121.0671; updates on CNAC activities; mentions [William L.] Bond, Admiral Shen Hung-leh, Chiang Kai-shek, Eddy Smith, [Paul] Groeger, Katherine Dunlop.
